items.stem: What is a realistic expectation when using a vision model on a poor-quality scanned document?

options.text: Accuracy can degrade, so outputs may need validation or human review
options.rationale: Correct: poor scans reduce accuracy and need safeguards.

options.text: It will always extract every field perfectly
options.rationale: Perfect extraction is not guaranteed on poor scans.

options.text: It cannot read any text at all
options.rationale: It can often read text, just with reduced accuracy.

options.text: It removes the need for a defined output schema
options.rationale: A schema is still needed for reliable downstream use.

items.explanation: Correct: poor scans reduce accuracy and need safeguards.

items.stem: Why request structured output (a defined schema) when extracting data from documents?

options.text: Downstream systems can consume consistent fields reliably
options.rationale: Correct: structured fields integrate cleanly downstream.
The image is still the source of the data.

options.text: It guarantees the model is always correct
options.rationale: A schema shapes output but does not guarantee correctness.

options.text: It removes the need to measure accuracy

items.stem: Which TWO safeguards make a document-extraction application more trustworthy? (Select TWO)

options.text: Validating extracted values such as checking a total
Routing low-confidence results to a human reviewer
options.rationale: Correct: a human-review path handles uncertain cases.

options.text: Publishing extracted numbers with no checks
options.rationale: Unchecked numbers are a reliability risk.

options.text: Measuring accuracy on no examples at all
options.rationale: Accuracy must be measured on labelled examples.
